answer: A berth-lock rule keeps fakes out: before bidding above ten units, an agent must hold one berth at the harbor jetty, locked for the whole job, so one identity runs one big bid at a time. Each hour the harbor publishes an echo of occupied berths, and two peers check it against new bids. Holding two berths, or bidding without one, burns an 18-unit bond each; honest agents moor once and work, while 100 fakes need 100 berths and risk 1,800 units.
